_doc: Which shared gates have PROVEN they can fail, and how.
READ BY checks/check_probes_pass.py, through checks/_calibration.py. Every entry is verified
against the estate before this file is believed: the key must name a gate that exists, a cited
prover must resolve and be COMMITTED, and a prover inside this repo must have had its claimed
self-proof run green by the same sweep. An entry naming no gate, no file, no commit or no
running proof is a FINDING (SUPERSOTA R7: a registry nothing reads is a rumour).
These gates run in four repos, so their proof belongs HERE rather than inside any one
consumer -- two of them were canaried from inside ZeroThunder, which meant the other three
inherited the gate without the evidence.
proven_by: the canary runs each check against a git repo containing a real violation and
asserts it goes RED, then against a clean tree and asserts GREEN. Red-on-violation is the
load-bearing half: a gate that scans nothing exits 0 and is indistinguishable from a gate
that scanned everything, and two fixtures in this very table were silently out of scope
Keys name the gate WITHOUT its check_ prefix, and a prose claim that names no prover file
(an in-selftest: entry) is left to the sweep rather than resolved here. Regenerate the canary
citations with the canary, never by hand -- a registry a human types is a registry that

proven_by.version_provenance: checks/check_version_provenance.py --probe (also pinned by tests/test_check_version_provenance.py): red on a version with no commit and no date; a version declared in src/lib.rs is REACHED (the widening -- narrowing MAIN_FILES back to src/main.rs goes red, and the checker reports not-applicable rather than a wrong verdict); an opaque clause field whose build script never asks about the working tree is red; a baseline entry naming a file the checker never reads is a FINDING; green on a truthful version
proven_by.lock_version: checks/check_lock_version.py --probe (also pinned by tests/test_check_lock_version.py): app_updates' real 2026-10-01 shape -- manifest 1.36.0, Cargo.lock 1.35.0, both members INHERITING -- is red; regenerating the lockfile is green; a release number bumped in one place only is red; per-crate versions are a layout and produce no finding; a member list spread over lines is read whole and an exclude below it is not mistaken for a member
proven_by.md_links: checks/check_md_links.py --probe (also pinned by tests/test_check_md_links.py): the audit's hand-mis-derived anchor (#48-what-90-can-actually-do-measured) is red and the right one is green; a missing file is red; a link in an inline code span, a fenced block or an indented block is an example and produces nothing
proven_by.no_empty_assert: checks/check_no_empty_assert.py --probe (also pinned by tests/test_check_no_empty_assert.py): every row of the measured clippy 1.99.0 table (2026-10-02) is a case -- the six shapes clippy reports AND the two it is silent on, `assert!(x.is_empty(), "msg")` and `assert!(!x.is_empty(), "msg")`, which is why the gate exists at all; the forms clippy tells you to write (`assert_eq!(x.len(), 0)`, `assert_ne!`) stay green; a multi-line chain is reported at its `assert!` line; a `)` inside a message does not end the scan; dropping the negation from the pattern turns the probe RED (tests/test_check_no_empty_assert.py::test_calibration_the_probe_goes_red_when_a_shape_is_dropped)
proven_by.tag_version: checks/check_tag_version.py --probe (also pinned by tests/test_check_tag_version.py): a pushed v<semver> tag whose commit declares another version is red; red on media_server's real 2026-10-01 shape (tag v1.79.3, commit declaring 1.79.1), green on a matching pair, and a tag with no version source is a finding
